newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi sees appliance business turning into black.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi sees appliance business turning into black.

text.p: Hitachi Ltd said on Friday its loss-making household electrical appliance business will turn into the black on a consolidated basis in the current business year, ending next March 31.

A company spokesman also told a news conference Hitachi will trim its group chip investment to 150 billion yen from an originally planned 175 billion yen for the current year, reflecting a softening of the memory chip market.
He said Hitachi expects the memory chip business to stay severe for the next two business years.
The spokesman said chip makers' production would shift into the next-generation 64 megabit DRAMs late next year, but Hitachi expected this business would also be very severe.

Hitachi is trying to increase production of MCU chips, used in household appliances, and concentrate less on memory chips for personal computers. In the current business year, memory chips account for 40 percent of its semiconductor business, and it is trying to reduce this ratio, he said.
